title: Automate ephemeral contractor seat provisioning via license-broker for PM/Analytics tools
content:
description:
Issue summary:
Request to build and enable an automated ephemeral-license broker integration that provisions time-limited SaaS seats (30-90 days) for contractors and vendor engineers across a small set of internal tools (Postgres monitoring, Looker Lite, Sentry non-prod, and a few analytics workspaces). The broker should:
- Accept requests from hiring managers or vendor owners via a lightweight self-serve form (ServiceNow or internal form).
- Create SCIM/SCIM-like provisioning events for Okta with a TTL tag and billing tag applied to the user or guest account.
- Emit events to billing (Chargeback tag), and create an audit trail for security/compliance.
Impact:
Current process is manual: Procurement + IT + Manager create accounts, track expiration in spreadsheets. This causes delays (2-5 business days), missed expirations (licensed overages), and inaccurate cost allocation. Automating will reduce lead time to < 1 day and prevent untagged seats that drive unbudgeted spend.
Background/context:
- Frequent temporary needs from Data Platform, Analytics, and Solutions Engineering for contractor access during 2–6 week sprints and vendor integrations.
- Recent Q4 audit found ~18 active contractor seats without cost-center tags.
- We have an internal repo (license-broker) prototype that issues SCIM PATCH events but lacks TTL enforcement and billing tagging.
Request details:
- Provision 100 ephemeral seats across vendors initially (breakdown: 40 Looker Lite, 30 Sentry non-prod seats, 20 Postgres monitoring seats, 10 misc analytics).
- Default TTL: 30 days; option for manager to select 14, 30, 60, or 90 days.
- Auto-remediate: 48 hours before expiry, notify manager; at expiry, deprovision via SCIM and create a ticket if deprovision fails.
- Billing: attach "cost_center" and "project_tag" metadata in provisioning event.
- Audit logs: write both provisioning and deprovisioning events to central audit bucket and Security runbook.
Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Self-serve form accepts request and creates a license-broker job within 15 minutes of submission.
- Okta receives SCIM provisioning with TTL and cost-center tags present.
- Billing portal shows tagged seats for chargeback within 48 hours.
- Automated deprovisioning occurs reliably for 90/60/30/14-day TTLs in test environment.
Cost estimate and procurement flow: 
- Initial one-off engineering effort estimated ~2.5 PE weeks.
- Expected license cost saving: avoid 18 untagged seats (~$1,600/mo) once automated.
- Procurement will need to negotiate a short-term bulk seat block or seek vendor-friendly 'ephemeral seats' per-vendor (if supported).
Preferred vendors/targets: Looker (Looker Lite), Sentry (non-prod org), Grafana Cloud (monitoring), Postgres monitoring vendor (pgwatch or equivalent).
Dependencies and constraints:
- Okta SCIM API rate limits and vendor SCIM implementations vary; some vendors require org-level API keys and can’t accept TTL metadata (workaround: use a housekeeping job that removes accounts after TTL).
- Billing integration requires a small ETL from audit events into Cost Center tagging pipeline (Finance sign-off required).
- Security wants approval to allow service-account-wide deprovision permission in Okta.
Security review:
- Security flagged need for: 1) least-privilege service account, 2) audit retention policy for ephemeral accounts, 3) an offboarding confirmation webhook.
Suggested rollout plan:
1) Integration proof-of-concept (staging): wire license-broker to Okta test tenant and one vendor (Sentry).
2) Pilot with Data Platform (10 seats) for 30 days.
3) Measure provisioning lead time, deprovision success rate, and billing tagging accuracy.
4) Iterate and expand to other vendors.
Links and references:
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/license-broker (PRs listed below)
- Recent audit notes: confluence.redwood.ai/display/AUD/Contractor+Seat+Audit+2025
- Security runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Ephemeral+Account+Controls


comments:
2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (reporter): Filed initial request after discussion with Data Platform lead; attached audit summary and estimated vendor breakdown.
2026-03-11 - Helena Ortiz (Procurement): Confirming vendor list and asking for preferred contract model — bulk seat block vs ad-hoc. Requested vendor MSA templates for Looker and Sentry.
2026-03-12 - Priya Desai (Security): Reviewed flow. Approved conceptually if we add least-privilege service account and 365-day audit retention for provisioning events. Asked for a threat model for deprovisioning failures.
2026-03-12 - Ravi Patel (assignee): Spun up staging license-broker and wired to Okta test tenant; initial SCIM PATCH works but Okta ignores custom TTL attribute — fallback plan: store TTL in license-broker DB and run housekeeper to remove after TTL.
2026-03-13 - Finance (Lucas Romero): Need to confirm whether chargeback tags can be inserted via SCIM or require post-processing; requested sample event schema. Asked for expected monthly spend with 100 ephemeral seats.
2026-03-14 - Ravi Patel: Pilot plan proposed. Next step: procurement to confirm vendor API keys and Finance to confirm billing ETL window. Linked PRs for staging changes created.
2026-03-14 - Maya Chen: Acknowledged and asked to prioritize Looker Lite because Data Platform onboarding requires Looker access for contractors starting 2026-04-01.

acceptance_criteria:
Self-serve form creates a valid license-broker job within 15 minutes
Okta receives a SCIM provisioning event with cost_center tag (or equivalent fallback recorded in audit) for each provisioned seat
Chargeback tags appear in billing portal within 48 hours of provisioning for pilot seats
Automated deprovision completes successfully for TTLs in staging for 14/30/60/90 day runs

next_steps:
Procurement (Helena) to confirm vendor API access and share MSA templates by 2026-03-18
Finance (Lucas) to validate billing ETL and confirm chargeback tagging approach by 2026-03-20
Engineering (Ravi) to complete staging integration with Sentry and run 14/30 day TTL tests by 2026-03-28
Security (Priya) to review service-account permissions once staging is wired (expected 2026-03-22)
